name: aiml-engineer-open-ended-grading-rubric
description: Rubric for silent LLM grading of open-ended (constructed-response) answers in the AI/ML Engineer adaptive assessment (CAT). Adapted from the Masar open-ended grading rubric, but bound to this bank's item fields and to IRT/CAT scoring.

applies_to.note: Every item carries open.question, open.answer_format, open.reference_answer, open.expected_answer_points, open.rubric_criteria, open.common_pitfalls, plus cat{a,b,c} and open.difficulty.

unit_interval.use: graded-response score fed to the CAT engine

scoring_frame.primary_skill_rule: The primary skill is the item's measures[0].variable (its sub-competency, e.g. C6.11). Grade the answer only against that competency; do not reward tangential knowledge from other competencies. Record the primary sub-competency and its parent competency on the result.

grader_settings.model_guidance: Use a strong reasoning model; grade silently — never reveal the reference answer or scores to the candidate.

output_schema.rationale: 2-4 sentence justification grounded in the criteria and the expected answer points

rubric_resolution_order: item.open.rubric_criteria[].descriptor  (primary: the per-item, question-specific standard for each of the four criteria)
item.open.expected_answer_points        (the discrete ideas a strong answer must contain; drives the completeness score)
item.open.reference_answer              (the gold-standard model answer; the accuracy yardstick)
grading_procedure: 1. Read item.open.question and item.open.answer_format so the answer is judged against what was actually asked and the expected form.
2. Match the candidate answer against item.open.expected_answer_points; record which points are covered and which are missed.
3. Match against item.open.common_pitfalls; record any pitfall the answer commits.

4. Score each of the four criteria on its own max using the item's per-criterion descriptor (rubric_resolution_order step 1), the covered/missed points, and the reference_answer as the accuracy yardstick.
5. raw_score = sum of the four criterion scores (0-20). Derive normalized_score = raw/4 and unit_score = raw/20.
6. Assign the verdict from verdict_thresholds using normalized_score.
7. Emit output_schema. Keep the rationale brief and evidence-based; never expose the reference answer to the candidate.

technical_accuracy.full: Every technical claim is correct and matches the reference answer's substance; correctly handles the core mechanism the question targets.
technical_accuracy.partial: Mostly correct with a minor error or imprecision that does not change the conclusion.
technical_accuracy.zero: A central claim is wrong, or the answer misidentifies the mechanism.
technical_accuracy.hard_cap: Each distinct common_pitfall the answer commits caps technical_accuracy at no more than 5, and two or more caps it at no more than 3.

completeness.rule: Score = round(5 * covered_points / total_expected_points), where points are item.open.expected_answer_points. Every required part of a multi-part question must be attempted for full marks.

reasoning_and_justification.full: Conclusions are argued from mechanism/trade-offs, not asserted; choices are justified against the alternatives the question raises.
reasoning_and_justification.zero: Only conclusions or recipes with no supporting reasoning.

clarity_and_communication.full: Well organised, precise terminology, directly answers the ask; a reviewer could act on it.
clarity_and_communication.zero: Disorganised or vague enough to obscure whether the candidate understands.

pitfall_handling.effect: Pitfalls are the constructed-response analogue of MCQ distractors. Committing one is direct evidence of a misconception: record it in pitfalls_triggered and apply the technical_accuracy hard_cap. A pitfall about a non-central detail may be noted without capping if the grader judges it peripheral to the question's target.

answer_channel_handling.text: Default. Grade the written answer directly with the frame above.
answer_channel_handling.voice_or_video_transcript: If an answer is captured as speech, transcribe first and grade the transcript with the identical rubric — spoken delivery is NOT judged here (mirrors Masar video.content_score using the voice rubric). Only introduce a separate delivery score if the platform explicitly collects one; it is out of scope for this text-first bank.
answer_channel_handling.note: All 107 items in this bank are text constructed-response; answer_channel is an extensibility hook, not a per-item property.

cat_integration.model: Items are pre-calibrated with cat{a,b,c}; open items use c = 0.0 (no guessing on constructed response), so the effective model is 2PL.
cat_integration.response_scoring: Feed unit_score (raw/20, in [0,1]) to the ability (theta) update as a graded/partial-credit response — open-ended items yield partial credit and should not be forced to 0/1 where the estimator supports polytomous scoring.
cat_integration.dichotomous_fallback: If the CAT engine expects a binary correct/incorrect (3PL/2PL dichotomous), dichotomize at unit_score >= 0.60 = correct, else incorrect, then apply the item's a/b with c = 0.0. The 0.60 threshold aligns with the 'knows' band boundary below.
cat_integration.difficulty_note: Item difficulty is already encoded in cat.b and open.difficulty; do NOT re-scale scores by difficulty during grading — the IRT model accounts for difficulty when updating theta.
cat_integration.exposure: Grade one item at a time; the CAT engine selects the next item by information at the current theta. This rubric governs only the per-item score.

guardrails.no_length_bias: Longer answers are not better. Reward substance that matches expected_answer_points, not verbosity.
guardrails.penalise_fabrication: Confident but incorrect specifics (invented numbers, non-existent APIs, wrong mechanisms) are scored as errors under technical_accuracy, never as completeness.
guardrails.answer_the_actual_ask: An answer that is correct about an adjacent topic but does not address the question's specific ask cannot exceed partial.
guardrails.reference_is_a_yardstick_not_a_key: The candidate need not match the reference answer's wording or every point; a materially correct, well-argued alternative that covers the expected points scores full marks.
guardrails.silent_grading: Never surface the reference answer, expected points, pitfalls, or scores to the candidate during the assessment.
